name: Bismarck
description: Bismarck is a Swedish three-player trick-taking game where players score based on the number of tricks they win compared to a 'quota.' Over 12 deals, each player must play each of four different contracts exactly once as forehand: Sang (no trumps, win tricks), Pass (no trumps, avoid tricks), Spader (spades trump), and Valfri (choose your trump suit). Similar to the Polish game Mizerka.

content.text: Bismarck is a Swedish three-player trick-taking game where players score based on the number of tricks they win compared to a 'quota.' Over 12 deals, each player must play each of four different contracts exactly once as forehand: Sang (no trumps, win tricks), Pass (no trumps, avoid tricks), Spader (spades trump), and Valfri (choose your trump suit). Similar to the Polish game Mizerka.

The first known description of Bismarck appeared in 1944 in Sweden. According to Sten Helmfrid (Kartofilen, July 2024), the game was likely named after the famous German battleship Bismarck, which was sunk in 1941 â€” making this a WW2-era card game.
Standard 52-card deck, no Jokers. Cards rank A-K-Q-J-10-9-8-7-6-5-4-3-2.
52-card deck. Score sheet with grid (rows: players, columns: contracts).

Dealer shuffles; player to dealer's right cuts. Dealer deals the top 4 cards face-up on the table, then deals the remaining 48 cards face-down to the three players (16 each). Forehand (left of dealer) picks up the 4 face-up cards (total 20 cards) and discards any 4 face-down.
